```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Parameters
n <- 48
phi <- 0.5
theta <- 0.45

# Components of the asymptotic variance formula
num_phi <- (1 - phi^2) * (1 - phi * theta)
num_theta <- (1 - theta^2) * (1 - phi * theta)
denom <- (phi - theta)^2

# 1. Evaluate Variances
var_phi <- (1/n) * (num_phi / denom)
var_theta <- (1/n) * (num_theta / denom)

# 2. Evaluate Correlation
# Correlation is independent of n in the asymptotic formula
cor_phi_theta <- -(sqrt(1 - phi^2) * sqrt(1 - theta^2)) / (1 - phi * theta)

# Display Results
cat("Variance of phi-hat: ", var_phi, "\n")
cat("Variance of theta-hat:", var_theta, "\n")
cat("Correlation:         ", cor_phi_theta, "\n")
```
The variances are massive > 4 relative to the parameter values 0.5 and 0.45. This occurs because the denominator $(\phi - \theta)^2$ is extremely small 0.0025. As $\phi$ approaches $\theta$, the variance tends toward infinity. The correlation is nearly -1. This indicates that the AR and MA components are nearly canceling each other out (the roots are too close). Mathematically, the model is almost indistinguishable from white noise. A sample of $n=48$ is insufficient to resolve such similar AR and MA components.


```{r}
n <- 120

# Components of the asymptotic variance formula
num_phi <- (1 - phi^2) * (1 - phi * theta)
num_theta <- (1 - theta^2) * (1 - phi * theta)
denom <- (phi - theta)^2

# 1. Evaluate Variances
var_phi <- (1/n) * (num_phi / denom)
var_theta <- (1/n) * (num_theta / denom)

# 2. Evaluate Correlation
# Correlation is independent of n in the asymptotic formula
cor_phi_theta <- -(sqrt(1 - phi^2) * sqrt(1 - theta^2)) / (1 - phi * theta)

# Display Results
cat("Variance of phi-hat: ", var_phi, "\n")
cat("Variance of theta-hat:", var_theta, "\n")
cat("Correlation:         ", cor_phi_theta, "\n")

```
Even though the variance is twice less than the first experiment, compared to the parameters, we still face the same issue.
